target_subject: a person's hands manipulating a mechanical watch movement with tools

scene: A dark, matte surface serves as the background for a disassembled gold-toned watch movement and several metal tools.
Two hands are positioned around the watch movement: one holding it steady, the other using tweezers near its upper edge.
Three slender metallic rods lie horizontally in the upper background, out of focus.
action: The left hand grips the outer rim of the circular watch movement, stabilizing it on the surface.
The right hand holds fine-tipped metal tweezers, positioning them just above the top jewel or pivot of the movement.
The watch movement is fully exposed, showing gears, bridges, and a visible balance wheel assembly.
rationale: The presence of specialized tools and the open state of the movement suggest maintenance or assembly rather than casual handling.
The precise grip and tool placement imply deliberate, controlled manipulation, though intent (repair vs. inspection) is not visually verifiable.
No text or branding is legible on the movement or tools, limiting identification of origin or model.
object: A circular, gold-colored mechanical watch movement with visible gear trains, a balance cock, and a central wheel train is centered in the frame.
Two human hands are visible: the left hand’s thumb and index finger encircle the movement’s perimeter; the right hand’s thumb and index finger hold silver-colored tweezers.
Three cylindrical metal tools—likely screwdrivers or pegwood holders—are arranged parallel in the background, blurred due to shallow depth of field.
The movement features at least two visible jewels (dark circular insets) and a hairspring coiled around the balance staff.
The surface beneath the objects is uniformly dark gray or black with a non-reflective, slightly textured finish.
